title: Video is made from images, not from text alone
finding: Nearly every recorded video job is bound to an image or frame; a declared text-to-video route never appears, and explicit empty-media video requests are a small residue.
frequency: Image-bound video jobs: 93.40% of the mean film's video jobs (pooled 94.57%, 36,417/38,508 jobs, 156 films). Empty-media candidates: 530 jobs in 82 films. Declared text-to-video: 0 jobs.
stage: Video generation; image-to-video and reference-guided video
evidence_note: Counts of recorded media bindings on video jobs.
strength: strong: whole primary population, deterministic record counts
study04_status: Study 08 conservative input route and direct candidate: confirmed. A job with no recorded input never establishes text-only production.
example_excerpt: [producer model] nano_banana_2 [consumer model] seedance_2_5 [explicit usage] asset_role reference_image
denominator: 38,508 primary video jobs in 156 video-bearing films
competing_explanation: The interface may encourage image upload first; unpublished text-only trials and history capture can shape routes; a bound image need not be the shot's start frame.
confidence_rationale: Deterministic compound-key counts of released usage rows; attached contents are not inspected.

title: Shots share sources and build on earlier outputs
finding: Most jobs use a source that another job also uses, and about half take an earlier job's output, so a film's history is a web of reuse rather than one-off requests. Single sources can feed very many jobs.
frequency: Mean film: shared-input jobs 70.89% (pooled 70.20%); chained jobs 52.71% (pooled 55.75%); both 50.60%. Material input assets used more than once: 69.08% per film (20,383/29,321 assets). The largest hub, one APEIROPHOBIA asset, has 1,602 distinct consumers.
stage: Across image and video work; inputs, references and chaining
evidence_note: Structure of the disclosed lineage graph. What a shared source means (same shot, same character) is not observed.
strength: strong for structure; meaning undecided
study04_status: Study 07 raw compound input reuse or branch, and Study 08 branches, chains and convergence: undecided. Text labels cannot show that shared inputs serve the same shot or entity.
example_excerpt: distinct consumers=1602; total asset input nodes=669
denominator: 130,704 primary jobs in 157 films; 29,321 material input assets in 156 films
competing_explanation: Omitted external or private work and unresolved cross-ID aliases change the topology; a shared input need not represent the same shot or entity; reuse is not approval.
confidence_rationale: Exact compound-key counts and deterministic traversal of released records; no media inspection.

title: Work passes between models
finding: A large share of jobs consume something a different model made, so films are assembled across several models rather than inside one. Handoffs are specific: most model pairs that appear in the same film never pass anything to each other.
frequency: Mean film: 36.92% of jobs take an input made by a different literal model (146 of 157 films). Resolved producer-consumer pairs crossing models: 140,008/198,201. Largest route: seedream_v5_pro to seedance_2_5, 30,119 pairs in 66 films. Co-occurring model pairs with any actual handoff: 353/1,472.
stage: Between image generation, video generation and finishing
evidence_note: Explicit producer-consumer bindings; co-occurrence alone is not a handoff.
strength: strong for the bindings; motive undecided
study04_status: Study 08 branches, chains, convergence and cross-model from explicit parents: undecided. Component overlap cannot prove a common shot or revision motive.
example_excerpt: [producer model] seedream_v5_pro [consumer model] gpt_image_2 [explicit usage] asset_role input_image
denominator: 130,704 primary jobs in 157 films; 198,201 resolved producer-consumer job pairs in 147 films; 1,472 unordered co-occurring model pairs
competing_explanation: Platform features may route outputs between models automatically; repeated requests and raw asset aliases change apparent handoffs; a binding is not approval.
confidence_rationale: Deterministic released-record counts; one consumer with several parents counts in several pairs.

title: Video requests are long and written out in full
finding: Video prompts are several times longer than image prompts and usually carry an attached input, a long description, camera wording and exclusion wording together. Provisional labels find most of the fourteen instruction components in a typical video text.
frequency: Median of per-film median prompt length: video 5,104 characters, image 1,549. All four traits together: 77.87% of the mean film's video prompts (pooled 81.48%; present in 150 of 156 films). Provisional components per text, mean film: video 12.5 of 14, image 8.2.
stage: Video generation prompts; image prompts for comparison
evidence_note: Lengths and the four-trait bundle are structural counts; the component counts are inferred from provisional 27B labels on a weighted sample.
strength: strong for length and bundle; moderate for component counts
study04_status: Study 06 lexical camera, lens, preservation and exclusion proxies: changed. The structural census stays; semantic components are a sampled, provisional addition.
example_excerpt: Six separate shots joined by five hard cuts ... tracking with her, handheld tremor ... Heavy rain falls in every frame.
denominator: 37,079 nonempty primary video prompts in 156 films; 87,238 nonempty primary image prompts in 155 films; component counts over successfully labelled sampled primary texts
competing_explanation: Templates, copied boilerplate and repeated batch text lengthen prompts without adding intent; the model or interface may reward long prompts; length is not quality.
confidence_rationale: The census reproduces Study 04's per-film counts exactly; component counts carry the provisional label agreement in L07.

title: Stills are made as foundations for video
finding: Some image jobs exist to be handed to video: their output is taken as an input by a video job. Separately, some jobs make images that are later attached as named references.
frequency: Image jobs whose output a video job takes: 14.91% of the mean film's image jobs (pooled 8.77%; 8,076/92,058 jobs; 143 of 155 films). Jobs whose output becomes a named reference: 3,930 jobs in 100 of 157 films.
stage: Image generation feeding video generation; reference preparation
evidence_note: Recorded bindings from image outputs into video jobs.
strength: strong
study04_status: Study 08 reference preparation and foundation distinct from verified sheet or keyframe: confirmed. A foundation is a recorded binding, not a verified keyframe.
example_excerpt: [producer model] gpt_image_2 [consumer model] seedance_2_5 [explicit usage] asset_role reference_image
denominator: 92,058 primary image jobs in 155 image-bearing films; 130,704 jobs in 157 films for reference preparation
competing_explanation: A video job may take an image as a loose reference rather than a frame; images used in video outside the platform are not recorded.
confidence_rationale: Deterministic binding counts; the role of the image inside the video is not inspected.

title: Few outputs are taken further, and video outputs least
finding: Only a minority of jobs have an output that any later job uses, and image outputs are taken further several times as often as video outputs.
frequency: Jobs whose output a later job uses: 14.74% of the mean film's jobs (pooled 12.07%; 15,781/130,704). Image 22.39% versus video 5.53% per film.
evidence_note: Further use is a recorded binding, not approval or selection.
strength: strong for the count; meaning limited
study04_status: Study 09 adoption is a recorded use measure; Study 04 leaves rerun-candidate motives undecided.
example_excerpt: [consumer text] Move the entire title "The Kiss" UP
denominator: 130,704 primary jobs in 157 films; 92,058 image and 38,508 video jobs
competing_explanation: Video may be assembled outside the platform, so unused video outputs may still be in the film; final edits and sound can happen elsewhere; batches inflate denominators; unpublished work is missing.
confidence_rationale: Deterministic counts over released bindings; no link from jobs to the final cut exists.

title: Batches repeat one request exactly
finding: Jobs launched together as a batch are the same request run several times: same text, same inputs, same model, and almost always the same controls. Variation comes from sampling, not from rewording.
frequency: Comparable batch pairs with identical text: 32,448/32,448. Pairs with changed inputs: 0; with changed controls: 18/32,980. Batch members: 25.07% of the mean film's jobs (pooled 38.66%). Exact repeat excess, the nonempty primary prompts beyond the first copy of each exact string: 38.45% per film.
stage: Image and video generation; candidate sampling
evidence_note: Exact text, input, model and control comparisons within recorded batches.
strength: strong
study04_status: Study 10 exact-string repeat excess: changed. A semantic duplicate or waste rate remains unavailable. Study 09 rerun-candidate motives: undecided.
example_excerpt: "controls_changed":0, "inputs_changed":0, "model_changed":0, "text_equal":1
denominator: 32,980 batch pairs in 111 films; 130,704 jobs and 124,449 nonempty primary prompts in 157 films
competing_explanation: The interface may create batches by default; a repeat may be a deliberate seed search, a retry after failure, or an accident; motives are not recorded.
confidence_rationale: Deterministic pair comparisons of released fields; hidden seeds and defaults are unknown.

title: Saying what must stay the same is far more common than keywords show
finding: Keyword counts of preservation wording miss most of it: provisional semantic labels find a request to keep something unchanged in about twice as many prompts. The gap is largest in video prompts.
frequency: Mean film: lexical preservation wording 31.78% of primary prompts; provisional semantic preservation 63.13%. Video: semantic 82.69% versus lexical 36.95%. Image: semantic 47.21% versus lexical 28.70%.
stage: Image edits and video generation prompts
evidence_note: Semantic shares come from provisional 27B labels on a weighted sample; lexical shares are observed counts.
strength: moderate: preservation agreement with the single-coder gold is high, but the sample excludes long texts
study04_status: Preservation and reference regex meanings in Studies 03, 05, 06, 07, 08 and 09: changed. Lexical counts stay; 27B preservation is an additional sampled measure with agreement and missingness bounds.
example_excerpt: The only change is a small mark of tomato ketchup on one side of his face ... EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS UNTOUCHED
denominator: 124,449 nonempty primary prompts in 157 films (lexical); weighted successful sample with covered stratum mass 55,609 (semantic)
competing_explanation: The labeller may read boilerplate continuity lines as preservation; the keyword list is English and narrow; long texts excluded from labelling may differ.
confidence_rationale: Study 04 weighting reproduced exactly here; semantic values carry failure bounds in Study 04's tables.

title: Several shots are asked for in words, not with the shot control
finding: When a video prompt describes several shots, the multi-shot control is almost always off; the shots are written into the prompt instead. The control itself is used in only a handful of films.
frequency: Video jobs with multi-shot wording and the control off: 8,981/9,060 (99.05% per film, 122 films). Control on: 170 jobs in 9 films.
evidence_note: Literal control values beside lexical shot wording.
strength: strong for the control state; shot intent of the wording is lexical
study04_status: Study 06 requested shots distinct from jobs and cuts: confirmed. Multi-shot lexical proxy: changed; no semantic label matches shot intent.
example_excerpt: EXACTLY TWO SHOTS ONLY — ONE SINGLE CUT. [literal controls] "multi_shots": false
denominator: 9,060 video jobs with multi-shot wording in 122 films; 38,508 video jobs in 156 films
competing_explanation: The control may be unavailable for some models or versions, or defaults may hide its state; wording can describe one shot's internal moves.
confidence_rationale: Literal control states and deterministic lexical matches; executed shots are not counted.

title: Sound is asked of the video model; separate audio and finishing jobs are rare
finding: Video jobs nearly always have sound generation switched on, while dedicated audio and voice jobs are rare. About half the films show finishing jobs such as editing or upscaling on the platform.
frequency: generate_audio on: 91.55% of the mean film's video jobs (35,905/38,508). Audio jobs: 132 in 10 films. Voice adapters: 61 jobs in 14 films. Finishing jobs: 1,358 in 80 of 157 films.
stage: Video generation controls; audio, voice and finishing
evidence_note: Literal control values and job roles.
strength: strong for what is recorded; external sound and editing are invisible
study04_status: Study 06 subject, camera, environment, events, audio and invariants in named spans: confirmed, without a dedicated audio label. Study 08 adapter mapping: undecided.
example_excerpt: Audio: Environmental SFX only. No music. No subtitles. [literal controls] "generate_audio": true
denominator: 38,508 video jobs in 156 films; 130,704 jobs in 157 films
competing_explanation: generate_audio may default to on; creators may discard generated sound and score externally; finishing done off-platform is not recorded.
confidence_rationale: Literal control states and deterministic role counts; sound is not heard.

title: Saved elements are reused
finding: Most films use saved reference elements, and most elements, once used, are used again.
frequency: Films using saved elements: 120 of 157. Used elements reused: 85.90% per film (pooled 88.02%; 4,577/5,200).
stage: Reference elements attached to image and video jobs
evidence_note: Recorded element attachments.
strength: strong for reuse counts; element identity undecided
study04_status: Study 03 disclosed record as element and semantic kind: undecided. Component presence cannot establish persistent identity or complete libraries.
example_excerpt: per-film used_elements and reused_elements
denominator: 5,200 used elements in 120 films
competing_explanation: Elements may be auto-attached by templates; the same character may live in several elements; libraries outside the workspace are not visible.
confidence_rationale: Deterministic counts of released attachments.

title: Folders do not follow what feeds what
finding: Nearly half of the recorded input bindings link jobs that sit in different, non-overlapping workspace folders, so folders are not a reliable map of a film's lineage.
frequency: Resolved input bindings across disjoint folders: 46.69% per film (pooled 54.19%; 147 films measured).
evidence_note: Folder placement compared across recorded bindings.
strength: moderate: folder meaning is creator-specific
study04_status: No Study 04 dependency.
example_film_id: all primary films with resolved bindings
example_excerpt: per-film disjoint-folder binding counts
denominator: 198,201 resolved bindings in 147 films
competing_explanation: Folders may group by scene, date or deliverable rather than lineage; moves after generation are not recorded.
confidence_rationale: Deterministic counts of released placements.

title: One video model carries most video work: seedance_2_5
finding: seedance_2_5 is the main video model in most films and usually makes nearly all of a film's video. It made every declared extension and most image-to-video jobs.
frequency: Top video model in 125 of 156 video-bearing films. Share of a film's video jobs: median 94.33%, mean 75.75%, pooled 80.72%; at least 90% in 90 films. Extensions: 2,260 jobs, all seedance_2_5 (100.00%). Image-to-video: 77.41% of the mean film's image-to-video jobs.
evidence_note: Literal model identifiers on recorded jobs. A preference is not observed.
strength: strong for the share; the reason is unknown (see L06)
study04_status: No Study 04 dependency for literal model counts.
example_excerpt: per-film video jobs, models, top_model and seedance_2_5_jobs
denominator: 38,508 video jobs in 156 films
competing_explanation: Availability, defaults, price, release timing and contest rules can concentrate use without any judgement of quality.
confidence_rationale: Deterministic counts over Study 08's model inventory.

title: Image work is spread over several models, led by three
finding: Films use several image models, and no single one dominates image work the way seedance_2_5 dominates video. For image jobs with an input, three models lead: nano_banana_2, seedream_v5_pro and gpt_image_2.
frequency: Image models per film: median 5 (IQR 3-8). Top image model's share of a film's image jobs: median 60.61%. Image jobs with an input, mean film share and films where top: nano_banana_2 33.28% (49), seedream_v5_pro 22.24% (44), gpt_image_2 20.96% (30).
evidence_note: Literal model identifiers on recorded image jobs.
strength: strong
study04_status: No Study 04 dependency for literal model counts.
example_excerpt: per-film image jobs, models and top_model
denominator: 92,058 image jobs in 155 films; 57,717 image jobs with an input in 153 films
competing_explanation: Model releases during the contest window, price and interface defaults shape the mix; films may switch models for reasons unrelated to the task.
confidence_rationale: Deterministic counts over Study 08's role matrix.

title: Two roles for image models: start from nothing, or work from what you give
finding: Two soul models, soul_cinematic and text2image_soul_v2, are almost always run without a recorded input and in batches, while nano_banana_2, seedream_v5_pro and gpt_image_2 usually receive an attached image and often combine several.
frequency: Per film using each model, no recorded input: soul_cinematic 88.87%, text2image_soul_v2 88.33%; batch members: 69.84% and 62.76%. Attached input: nano_banana_2 77.01%, seedream_v5_pro 75.51%, gpt_image_2 75.87%; two or more inputs: 34.15%, 35.88%, 34.58%.
stage: Image generation: first looks versus edits and composites
evidence_note: Recorded input bindings and batch membership per literal model.
strength: strong
study04_status: Study 08 conservative input route: confirmed. No recorded input never establishes text-only production.
example_film_id: all primary films using each model
example_excerpt: metric, model_identifier, films_using_model, equal_film_mean
denominator: Jobs of each model in films using it: soul_cinematic 7,696 in 65 films; text2image_soul_v2 5,809 in 56; nano_banana_2 25,355 in 138; seedream_v5_pro 21,136 in 96; gpt_image_2 14,397 in 120
competing_explanation: Interfaces differ: a model may not accept inputs, or may batch by default; the role is an affordance as much as a choice.
confidence_rationale: Deterministic counts per literal model; model versions and hidden defaults are not resolved.

title: Video foundations come from the three input-taking image models
finding: When an image is handed to video generation, seedance_2_5 almost always receives it, and the image was usually made by nano_banana_2, gpt_image_2 or seedream_v5_pro. The text-first soul_cinematic rarely makes foundations.
frequency: Image-to-video handoffs (111,297 pairs, 143 films), mean film share: consumer seedance_2_5 79.30%; producers nano_banana_2 27.41%, gpt_image_2 24.73%, seedream_v5_pro 21.64% (pooled 29.40%). soul_cinematic's share of image foundations: 3.53% per film.
evidence_note: Explicit producer-consumer bindings by literal model.
strength: strong
study04_status: Study 08 foundation distinct from verified keyframe: confirmed.
example_excerpt: [producer model] nano_banana_2 [consumer model] seedance_2_5
denominator: 111,297 image-to-video producer-consumer pairs in 143 films; 8,076 foundation image jobs in 143 films
competing_explanation: Producers reflect which models a film used for images at all; a foundation may be one of many candidate images.
confidence_rationale: Deterministic counts of Study 08's transitions by model type.

title: On-platform finishing runs through cinematic_video_editor
finding: Where finishing jobs exist, cinematic_video_editor is the usual tool, mostly fed by seedance_2_5 clips; topaz_video appears in fewer films but handles large volumes where used.
frequency: Of 80 films with finishing jobs, cinematic_video_editor is used in 73 and is the top finishing model in 66 (80.09% mean film share). topaz_video: 17 films, 31.15% of pooled finishing jobs. seedance_2_5 produces 60.96% of the mean film's into-finishing pairs.
evidence_note: Literal model identifiers on finishing jobs and their recorded inputs.
strength: moderate: about half the films show no on-platform finishing
study04_status: Study 08 closed adapter role mapping: undecided. What the editor does is not validated.
example_excerpt: [producer model] seedance_2_5 [consumer model] cinematic_video_editor [explicit usage] asset_role input_video
denominator: 1,358 finishing jobs in 80 films; 1,367 into-finishing pairs in 77 films
competing_explanation: Most editing is said to happen in external editors, so on-platform finishing is a partial view.
confidence_rationale: Deterministic counts; finishing content is not inspected.

title: Recorded seedance_2_5 settings: 720p or 1080p, wide frames, varied lengths
finding: seedance_2_5 jobs are mostly set to 720p or 1080p and to 16:9, with a large minority at 21:9. Clip lengths vary widely, with peaks at 20, 30 and 15 seconds.
evidence_note: Literal top-level control values.
strength: strong for recorded values; defaults unknown
study04_status: Study 09 top-level scalar control subset: confirmed. Hidden defaults and nested semantics remain unknown.
example_excerpt: per-film seedance_2_5 resolution, aspect_ratio and duration states
denominator: 31,080 seedance_2_5 jobs with valid control documents in 145 films
competing_explanation: Defaults, credit cost per second and resolution, and contest delivery specs shape settings.
confidence_rationale: Literal recorded values; jobs without a control value are kept separate in Study 06.

title: Outputs of the input-taking image models are taken further most often
finding: Outputs of gpt_image_2, seedream_v5_pro and nano_banana_2 are reused by later jobs more often than those of soul_cinematic or seedance_2_5.
frequency: Jobs whose output a later job uses, mean film share among films using the model: gpt_image_2 24.94%, seedream_v5_pro 22.57%, nano_banana_2 18.72%, soul_cinematic 10.02%, seedance_2_5 5.85%.
evidence_note: Recorded further use per literal model; not approval.
strength: moderate: batches and external assembly shift denominators
study04_status: Study 09 rerun-candidate motives: undecided.
example_excerpt: adopted and jobs by film and model_identifier
denominator: Jobs of each model in films using it: gpt_image_2 14,397 in 120 films; seedream_v5_pro 21,136 in 96; nano_banana_2 25,355 in 138; soul_cinematic 7,696 in 65; seedance_2_5 31,082 in 145
competing_explanation: Video outputs are assembled outside the platform; soul_cinematic runs in large batches, so most candidates are siblings; use is not quality.
confidence_rationale: Deterministic counts from Study 09.

title: Name the change, then name what must stay
finding: Edit requests usually say both what to change and what to leave alone, often with a hard boundary such as "ONLY" and "stays exactly unchanged". What is protected is often identity.
frequency: Image edit prompts with preservation wording: 56.71% of the mean film's edit prompts versus 30.46% of all its image prompts (146 films; pooled 62.69% versus 31.04%). Provisional: image texts asking to preserve mention identity 74.67% of the time versus 58.85% overall.
evidence_note: Co-occurrence of edit and preservation wording within prompts; the case shows the wording; the identity pair uses provisional labels.
strength: strong for the co-occurrence; benefit untested
study04_status: Study 05 edit, preservation and short-edit proxies: changed. Semantic preservation is conditional on the weighted sample; edit intent is not a released component.
example_excerpt: Edit: inside the CRT screen ONLY ... EVERYTHING outside the screen glass stays exactly unchanged
denominator: 23,074 image edit prompts in 146 films against 87,238 nonempty image prompts in 155 films; sampled successful image texts for the identity pair
competing_explanation: Templates may bundle edit and keep phrases; the keyword lists overlap in wording; whether naming invariants helps is untested.
confidence_rationale: Census-level co-occurrence reproduced from released features; provisional labels for the identity pair.

title: Prepare a reference package, then attach it
finding: Creators make dedicated reference images, typically several views of the same character or costume, and later attach them to image and video jobs. A prepared sheet can itself be edited for a variant.
frequency: Panel films preparing multi-angle references: 10 of 16, plus 1 that also prepared a location board. Jobs whose output becomes a named reference: 3,930 in 100 of 157 films. Jobs with a named reference attached: 32.67% of the mean film's jobs.
stage: Reference preparation before image and video generation
evidence_note: Panel prompts requesting sheets and recorded attachments; the sheet's form is not verified.
strength: moderate: purposive panel of 16; population counts are bindings only
study04_status: Study 03 package request or attachment distinct from fulfilment: confirmed. No sheet form is verified.
example_excerpt: Character reference sheet of the SAME person ... One FRONT view ... one BACK view
denominator: 16 panel films; 130,704 jobs in 157 films
competing_explanation: Sheets may be made for pitching or style exploration rather than consistency; whether a sheet beats a text description is untested.
confidence_rationale: Single-coder panel coding with scoped excerpts; deterministic population counts.

title: Write cuts and timing into the prompt
finding: Video prompts lay out shots and timings in words, with counted cuts and timestamps, even when the multi-shot control is off (see P09).
frequency: Provisional timing component in 89.41% of the mean film's video texts. Lexical multi-shot wording in 25.01% of the mean film's video prompts (pooled 24.43%).
evidence_note: Case wording is observed; the timing share is inferred from provisional labels.
strength: moderate: instruction only; executed cuts are not counted
study04_status: Study 06 requested shots distinct from jobs and cuts: confirmed. Study 06 possible conflicts between timing text and controls: confirmed, unadjudicated.
example_excerpt: Six separate shots joined by five hard cuts ... 4.0s HARD CUT
denominator: Sampled successful video texts in 156 films (timing); 37,079 nonempty video prompts in 156 films (lexical)
competing_explanation: The model may ignore timings; writers may copy timing templates; timing text and the duration control may disagree.
confidence_rationale: Provisional label agreement for timing is reported in Study 04; lexical counts are deterministic.

title: Give the camera, the subject and the world their own sentences
finding: Detailed video prompts describe what the camera does, what the subject does and what the environment does in separate statements, rather than one blended description.
frequency: Provisional components in the mean film's video texts: camera motion 90.53%, action 96.54%. Lexical camera wording: 86.28% of the mean film's video prompts (pooled 87.47%).
evidence_note: Case wording is observed; component shares are inferred from provisional labels.
strength: moderate: separation is shown in cases; shares only show presence
study04_status: Study 06 subject, camera, environment, events, audio and invariants in named spans: confirmed, without a dedicated environment-motion label.
example_excerpt: tracking with her, handheld tremor ... Roopa hauls right to left ... Heavy rain falls in every frame.
denominator: Sampled successful video texts in 156 films; 37,079 nonempty video prompts in 156 films
competing_explanation: Presence of both components does not show they were separated; separation may be a writing habit with no effect on output.
confidence_rationale: Provisional labels; lexical counts deterministic.

title: Say what each reference is allowed to decide
finding: Some creators state the scope of a reference's authority, for example that one image governs the whole shot, instead of leaving the model to weigh several inputs.
frequency: Panel films with a creator-declared reference authority: 9 of 16.
evidence_note: The creator's own instruction about a reference; whether the model obeys is not observed.
strength: weak to moderate: purposive panel only
study04_status: Study 03 property location in prose or metadata with unknown media: confirmed.
example_excerpt: This single reference image is authoritative for the entire shot.
denominator: 16 panel films
competing_explanation: Authority wording may be boilerplate; panel selection is purposive; no population census of authority wording exists.
confidence_rationale: Single-coder panel coding; 7 of 16 panel films could not be coded.

title: Put exclusions inside the main prompt
finding: The separate negative-prompt field is almost unused; creators write what they do not want, such as music, voices or subtitles, into the main prompt instead.
frequency: Nonempty negative-prompt fields: 2 in 2 films. Exclusion wording in the mean film's prompts: video 90.87%, image 67.84%. Provisional exclusion component in video texts: 91.48%.
evidence_note: Field states and lexical counts; the component share is inferred from provisional labels.
strength: strong for field use; exclusion wording is broad
study04_status: Study 06 lexical exclusion proxy: changed. It gains a provisional sampled semantic measure.
example_excerpt: "camera":"locked frame on the dial and hands" ... no voice, no music
denominator: Negative-role fields in all 157 films; 37,079 nonempty video and 87,238 nonempty image prompts
competing_explanation: The negative field may be hidden in the interface for most models; exclusion keywords include common words in other senses.
confidence_rationale: Deterministic field and lexical counts; provisional semantic share.

title: Continue from the previous clip
finding: To carry action across clips, creators feed an earlier video back in, either guiding a new clip from it or declaring an extension, and say where to pick up.
frequency: Films with video guided by an earlier video: 113 of 156 video-bearing films. Declared extensions: 2,260 jobs in 53 films.
evidence_note: Recorded video inputs and declared extension mode.
strength: strong for the routes; continuity achieved is not observed
study04_status: Study 07 raw input reuse or branch: undecided.
example_excerpt: frame 1 same last frame from here <<<video_1>>>
denominator: 38,508 video jobs in 156 films
competing_explanation: Video inputs may be used for style or motion transfer rather than continuation; extension availability depends on the model.
confidence_rationale: Deterministic route counts; the media are not inspected.

title: Combine source images and give each one a job
finding: Composite image requests attach several images and say what to take from each, sometimes as an ordered checklist of properties to match.
frequency: Image jobs combining two or more inputs: 28.94% of the mean film's image jobs (pooled 30.63%; 150 of 155 films).
evidence_note: Recorded multi-input bindings; the ordered checklist is case wording.
strength: strong for multi-input use; checklist wording is case-scoped
study04_status: Study 05 integration properties and sheet, plate or poster purpose in cases: confirmed.
example_excerpt: TRANSPLANT THE PLANT FROM IMAGE 2 ONTO THE SHELF. FIRST, SCALE. SECOND, POSITION. THIRD, VIEWING ANGLE. FOURTH, LIGHTING.
denominator: 92,058 image jobs in 155 films
competing_explanation: Multiple inputs may be alternative candidates rather than parts; masks and layers are not recorded (L08).
confidence_rationale: Deterministic binding counts; single-coder case reading.

title: Short edits ride on an attached image
finding: Very short edit requests are almost always attached to an image and rarely use camera language; the image carries the context and the text names only the change.
frequency: Short image edits (4,116 prompts in 98 films) with an attached image: 98.39% per film versus 71.22% for all image prompts in those films (pooled 4,089/4,116). With camera wording: 4.81% versus 40.49%.
evidence_note: Co-occurrence of the short-edit proxy with recorded attachments and camera wording.
strength: strong for the association
study04_status: Study 05 short-edit proxy: changed. Edit intent is not a released semantic component.

finding: About a third of prompts use section labels, such as foreground, middle ground and background, to organise a description. Machine-style JSON prompts are rare.

denominator: 124,449 nonempty primary prompts in 157 films; 87,238 image and 37,079 video prompts
competing_explanation: Section labels may come from templates or prompt-writing tools; labels in other languages are missed.

title: Revise a clip by naming the fix and keeping the rest
finding: Video revisions bound to an earlier clip ask for a specific fix and say everything else stays; video edit wording comes with preservation wording more often than other video prompts do.
frequency: Video edit prompts with preservation wording: 50.74% of the mean film's edit prompts versus 38.33% of its video prompts (148 films).

strength: moderate

denominator: 12,676 video edit prompts in 148 films
competing_explanation: Edit words also describe in-scene actions; revisions outside the platform are invisible.
confidence_rationale: Census-level association from released features; single-coder case reading.

finding: Every technique above is an instruction or a binding, not an outcome: no output was watched or judged. Testing them needs Study 12's controlled experiments, for example a reference sheet against a text description of identity, staged against one-pass generation, a local edit against regeneration, and continuing from a last frame against re-referencing.

title: Failure, retry and discard rates
finding: The records hold no failure, rejection or approval state. Outputs that were not taken further are not failures, and rerun candidates have unknown motives.
frequency: Only 14.74% of the mean film's jobs are taken further; the rest have no recorded use, which is not the same as failure. Rerun candidates: 31.05% of the mean film's jobs, motive unknown.

study04_status: Study 09 equal-request rerun candidates: undecided. Motives need human validation.

title: Labour, cost and speed
finding: Timestamps show when recorded jobs ran, not how long anyone worked, and no credits or costs are recorded. Spans and active dates are not effort measures.

denominator: 157 films

title: Semantic findings rest on a provisional sample
finding: The instruction-component findings come from one local model's provisional labels on a stratified sample, with long texts excluded and agreement measured against a single coder. A multilingual, adjudicated census would be needed to treat them as more than provisional.

finding: Versions of an element are inferred from lineage, not declared, and nothing marks an output as approved. Whether two records are the same asset under different IDs is undecided.
